title: GPU pool queue triage and autoscaler safeguards roadmap
creator: Ava Martinez
description: After the Feb 2025 hosted-api capacity event, we observed prolonged GPU queue buildup and throttling on multiple pools. This ticket tracks the triage work, short-term mitigations, and medium-term autoscaler / admission changes required to prevent recurrence and reduce customer impact. Focus areas: scaling signal stability, admission scoring, tenant burst containment, prewarm behavior, and synthetic load validation.
postmortem_summary: Root cause was multi-factor: (1) autoscaler reaction function used instantaneous queued-length spikes, leading to oscillatory prewarm and missed steady-state capacity; (2) prewarm priming created many short-lived slots that looked available but produced high scheduling overhead; (3) tenant KV-cache pollution allowed a small set of tenants to occupy disproportionate GPU residency during bursts, amplifying queue buildup for others; (4) admission logic lacked an explicit tenant burst cap and scoring for long-running token streams, so fairness broke under heterogeneous workloads. Monitoring gaps: no synthetic tenant-fairness test and insufficient telemetry on 'active sequences' vs 'queued requests'.
action_items: SHORT-TERM: Deploy emergency soft-cap on per-tenant RPS during warm window (owner: Ravi Singh) - deadline 2025-02-21
SHORT-TERM: Rollback prewarm aggressiveness by halving priming batch size and increase scale-up cooldown to 90s (owner: Infra Ops) - deadline 2025-02-22
SHORT-TERM: Enable fallback routing to quantized-compatible model variant for best-effort requests when pool queue > 80% (owner: Model Ops) - deadline 2025-02-25
MEDIUM-TERM: Change autoscaler primary signal from instantaneous queued-length to 60s moving-average of active_sequences + queued_length (owner: Capacity Eng) - deadline 2025-03-07
MEDIUM-TERM: Implement tenant burst window with decay counter (slot reservation decay) to prevent long-lived reservation hoarding (owner: Scheduling Team) - deadline 2025-03-14

MEDIUM-TERM: Add admission scoring that factors request sequence-length-estimate, tenant-credit, and cache-hit-likelihood to prefer short, cache-friendly requests under pressure (owner: Runtime Eng) - deadline 2025-03-21
MEDIUM-TERM: Instrument telemetry for active_sequence_count and reservation_age; add dashboards and SLO alerts (owner: Observability) - deadline 2025-03-07
LONG-TERM: Build synthetic tenant-fairness load generator and include in chaos/perf tests for release gating (owner: SRE + Perf) - deadline 2025-04-01
LONG-TERM: Introduce slot preemption policy for soft-fail overcommit scenarios with graceful ejection and replay hints (owner: Runtime Eng) - deadline 2025-04-15
comments: 2025-02-10 - Ava Martinez: Initial triage notes collected from oncall and logs. GPU pool 'us-west-2-pool-7' sustained >85% queue for 18 minutes during peak. Created this ticket to coordinate follow-ups.

2025-02-11 - Ravi Singh: Emergency mitigation rolled: increased temporary target capacity for hot pools and introduced per-tenant soft RPS cap. Early telemetry shows tail latency improved ~40% for impacted tenants.

2025-02-12 - Maya Chen (SRE): Investigated prewarm traces; prewarm churn accounted for 12% of CPU scheduling overhead and correlated with autoscaler oscillation. Proposed cooldown changes recorded in PR #7852.

2025-02-14 - Jonas Becker (Runtime Eng): Drafted admission scoring proposal. Key trade-off: over-penalizing long-running streams harms batch throughput for embeddings. Need an A/B test to tune weights.

2025-02-18 - Product PM (Lena Ortiz): Customer-impacted tenants were primarily mid-market with bursty conversational workloads. PM requests explicit SLA mitigation path and communication plan for affected customers.
2025-02-20 - Ravi Singh: Added medium-term autoscaler spike smoothing RFC to the docs. Plan to land in runtime-1.21 canary and run synthetic fairness test before broad rollout.
